metadata.description: Multi-chat orchestration for Claude Code. Two release channels: install `claude-bridge` for the stable channel (recommended), or `claude-bridge-dev` to try the next release early. Install one, not both.

plugins.name: claude-bridge
plugins.description: STABLE CHANNEL — recommended. MCP server for cross-Claude-Code-chat orchestration plus an optional control-plane daemon. Peer messaging and discovery, chat read/search across sessions, live context and rate-limit monitoring via a chained statusLine wrapper and a PostToolUse OAuth hook, context and rate-limit guards, idle-beep notification, bundled role skills. The opt-in daemon (`install --systemd`) supervises peer lifecycle: spawn/stop/restart with sanitized env and a fork-guard, peer_compact orchestration (audited inject path, auto-watchdog off by default), team_layout declarative reconcile, lifecycle events routed into offline peers' inboxes. Without the daemon the plugin behaves exactly as before — no regression. See docs/SETUP-DAEMON.md and ADR-008 in docs/architecture.md.

plugins.name: claude-bridge-dev
plugins.description: DEVELOPMENT CHANNEL — ahead of stable, proven in daily operation on a 23-peer fleet but not yet promoted. Everything the stable channel has, plus what is being prepared for the next release. Do NOT install alongside `claude-bridge`: both register an MCP server and you would run two side by side. Pick this only if you want changes early and can tolerate breakage; otherwise install `claude-bridge`. Ahead of stable with: team_stop (controlled sleep of a whole team via a stop-request/ack protocol) and team_layout resuming peers it put to sleep; a re-entrancy guard and claim-before-dispatch on the daemon's request loop, with timeouts on every tmux call; workspace hygiene (orphaned temp files, retention sweeps) and survival of EPIPE in the statusLine chain. v0.10.2 fixed four tools that reported results they had never checked — peer_restart claiming a start it had not performed, peer_spawn accepting a session with no process in it, model_info serving a model table that had drifted from what Anthropic publishes (a 1M model listed at 200k, a price 50% high), and session_stats undercounting a transcript by 13% because it validated while counting. See CHANGELOG.md, docs/SETUP-DAEMON.md and ADR-008 in docs/architecture.md. v0.10.3 follows on: peer_restart now relaunches a peer with the command and arguments it was actually given, instead of a hardcoded `claude` that only resolves when the daemon's PATH happens to contain it.
